title: Fourth Floor Walk-Up
mood: earnest, out of breath, falling hard
subject: carrying a friend's sofa up four flights of a walk-up and realising on the third landing that you are in love with her
caption: Arena piano pop-rock power ballad. Solo grand piano under a close-miked raspy male vocal for the first verse; floor-tom pulses entering at the pre-chorus; a big reverb-heavy snare on two and four from the first chorus; distorted power-chord guitars and a string section arriving at the bridge, with stacked gang vocals and a lift up a whole step for the last chorus. Starts dry and intimate and builds wide and roomy, the voice always forward. Male voice, a raspy tenor, intimate and nearly spoken in the verses, belting with falsetto cracks at the climax. 74 BPM, D major. Earnest, out of breath, falling hard. No trap drums, no EDM drop, no autotune, no country twang, no gospel organ.
lyrics:
[Intro - solo grand piano]

[Verse 1]
You said it's just a couch, it'll take ten minutes
It's a green velvet sleeper and it weighs about a ton
Fourth floor walk-up on Delancey, no elevator
You took the top end, so I've got all the weight

[Pre-Chorus - floor toms enter]
Second landing, it gets stuck on the rail
You start laughing and you can't stop

[Chorus - full drums]
I fell for you on the third floor landing
Holding half a sofa with my knees and my chin
You laughed so hard you had to sit down on it
And I didn't want it to fit

[Verse 2]
We took the legs off with a butter knife
Tipped it on its end and it slid around the turn
Mr. Ocampo from 3B held the door with his slipper
Said "you two been married long?" And neither of us said no

[Bridge - strings and power chords build]
Ten years I've known you, I've moved you four times
First time I ever wished there were more stairs to climb

[Chorus - lifted a whole step, gang vocals]
I fell for you on the third floor landing
Holding half a sofa with my knees and my chin
The legs are still in my jacket pocket
So I'll have to come back and screw them in

[Outro - solo piano]
Four floors down and still out of breath
You said bring the legs back Saturday
